findings.title: UserErrorResponse declares a string message, but the endpoint emits an Error object on failures
findings.evidence: The POST response annotation selects UserErrorResponse for 500 (target/src/servers/sample.typescrit.swagger.api/controllers/controller.user.ts:41). Its message is decorated and typed string (target/src/modules/users/models/user.ts:37-40). StoreUser.get rejects the database error unchanged (target/src/modules/users/services/stores/store.user.ts:52-56); ServiceUser.find catches that value and passes it directly to ResponseFailure(500, error) (target/src/modules/users/services/service.user.ts:95-96). ResponseFailure assigns message without normalization (target/src/modules/common/utils/response.ts:52-57), and ControllerUser.find sends the resulting object unchanged (target/src/servers/sample.typescrit.swagger.api/controllers/controller.user.ts:61). Its own catch does the same with ex at line 65. For a native Error, JSON serialization emits the exact top-level field list code,error,message with message:{}; it never emits the Error.message text as a string. review/correctness-reproduction.json records an isolated extraction of the actual ResponseFailure function body and JSON.stringify result. The request validator also assigns a Joi error object to message before res.json for a 400 (target/src/modules/common/utils/validation.ts:49-55), providing a second reachable producer of the same schema mismatch. An SDK or schema validator expecting message:string can reject the response rather than handle the documented error.
findings.counterexample: Condition: StoreUser.get rejects with new Error("DB unavailable"). The source catch path returns ResponseFailure(500,error), and the isolated extracted response function produces JSON {"code":500,"error":"Internal Server Error","message":{}}. The advertised UserErrorResponse requires any supplied message to be a string. No live server, database or HTTP reproduction was run; Express serialization and Swagger generation remain runtime verification work.
findings.rationale: This is an API contract incompatibility on the documented 500 error path, not a request to expose internal exception text. Normalize or omit message consistently with the schema, and use an appropriate documented structure for validation details.

scope.target_type: existing API specification; not a diff
scope.reviewed: Swagger route responses and UserResponse/UserErrorResponse, ServiceUser.find, StoreUser.get, database findOneById boundary, ResponseSuccess/ResponseFailure/IModelResponse; required request validation and serialization call sites.
value_trace: Producer: FindUserByIdRequest exposes one required string userId (models/user.ts:133-139). The controller reads req.body.userId for comparison with decodedToken.userId, then forwards req.body (controller.user.ts:50-56). StoreUser.get consumes only userId; database findOneById converts it to ObjectID and queries _id (service.mongo.db.client.ts:42-44).

Storage boundary: StoreUser.get resolves the database document unchanged (store.user.ts:50-58). A TypeScript ModelUser annotation does not project fields. ServiceUser.find deletes exactly emailVerificationId,password,oldPasswords,accessToken, then passes all remaining own properties to ResponseSuccess (service.user.ts:83-92).

Success serializer boundary: ResponseSuccess instantiates empty IModelResponse and assigns exactly code,data (response.ts:32-36; i.model.response.ts:1-6); controller res.send(resp) at line 61 delegates object serialization to Express. Top-level fields are code,data. Within data, the field list is database own enumerable keys minus the four explicit deletions; no whitelist exists. For a document containing exactly the declared ModelUser properties, remaining keys are _id,uuidMobile,mobileToken,firstname,lastname,email,birthDate,phoneNumber,address,claims,photoUrl,enable,emailVerified,gender,godfatherCode,facebookId,facebookAccessToken,pubToken,push,isAdmin,passwordVerificationId. Nested declared address fields: country,state,city,address; push fields: userIdOneSignal,pushToken. Stored extra properties would also be emitted. ObjectID JSON behavior depends on the unavailable MongoDB runtime.

Receiving success contract: UserResponse decorates code,data and refers data to ModelUser (models/user.ts:11-24). The ModelUser documentation includes accessToken,emailVerificationId, which this endpoint always deletes, but those properties are optional, so their omission alone is not a finding. No downstream client implementation is in the authorized scope.

Failure serializer boundary: ResponseFailure assigns exactly code,error,message, with error a status description and message the supplied value (response.ts:52-57). String-producing not-found/forbidden branches conform; Error-producing catches do not conform to the receiving UserErrorResponse.message:string (models/user.ts:31-45). Native Error has no enumerable message property, so native JSON emits message:{}. No data property is assigned.

Actual serialization entry points found: controller res.status(resp.code).send(resp), its catch .send(ResponseFailure(...)), and validator res.json(response). No application JSON replacer or custom user toJSON was found in the scoped code. Installed Express implementation and generated Swagger were unavailable and were not fetched or installed.
scope.excluded: Other routes; neighboring credentials/configuration; security/feasibility candidates; live server, dependency installation and HTTP requests.

unfinished: No generated Swagger inspection or installed Express/MongoDB runtime serialization execution; isolated native JSON surrogate only. No downstream consumer is present in the scoped artifact.
